# Adjudication Task — Chapter 182

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃182화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|저벅. 저벅.
  6|
  7|수많은 사람의 시선 속, 두 사람이 서로를 향해 걸음을 옮겼다. 마침내 마주 선 그들은 상대방을 향해 포권을 취했다.
  8|
  9|“태원진가의 진위경이라 하오.”
 10|
 11|“화산의 백무성입니다.”
 12|
 13|화산파. 그리고 백무성.
 14|
 15|이 두 단어가 가진 파급력은 어마어마했다.
 16|
 17|사방에서 터져 나온 탄성이 적막을 순식간에 걷어 냈다.
 18|
 19|“화산파!”
 20|
 21|“백무성, 화산일학 백무성이다!”
 22|
 23|비록 양민들이 섞여 있다고는 하나, 오늘 이 자리에 모인 이들은 상당수가 무림인이다.
 24|
 25|화산파라는 배경, 그리고 화산일학이라는 별호가 가지는 무게감은 어마어마했다.
 26|
 27|“세상에, 화산일학이 왜 여기에 왔지?”
 28|
 29|“태원진가의 위세가 이 정도였나?”
 30|
 31|“자, 잠깐, 화산일학이 여기 왔다는 건…….”
 32|
 33|정신없이 떠들어 대던 사람들이 주위를 훑었다. 얼마 지나지 않아 백무성의 곁에 있는 일남일녀를 발견하고는 다시 한번 탄성이 새어 나왔다.
 34|
 35|“저 청년이 패화권(敗花拳)인가 보군. 듣던 대로 덩치가 어마어마해.”
 36|
 37|“화검봉(花劍鳳)도 있다! 심지어 예뻐!”
 38|
 39|“우와아아! 매화삼절이다!”
 40|
 41|생각 이상으로 대단한 관심에 철우와 은향이 어리둥절한 표정을 지었다.
 42|
 43|두 사람 모두 몇 번인가 사부인 천검진인을 따라 강호에 나온 적은 있지만 이 정도의 환호를 받는 건 처음이었다.
 44|
 45|“뭐야, 내가 이렇게 유명했나? 별호도 알고 있는데?”
 46|
 47|“철 오라버니, 들었어요? 누가 방금 나보고 예쁘대요.”
 48|
 49|철우가 정색하며 대답했다.
 50|
 51|“잘못 들은 거니까 일절 신경 쓰지 마라.”
 52|
 53|“……짜증 나, 진짜.”
 54|
 55|어린 시절부터 동문수학하며 친남매처럼 자란 두 사람이다. 눈빛으로 으르렁거리는 두 사람의 모습에 진위경이 잔잔하게 웃었다.
 56|
 57|“사이가 좋아 보이는구려.”
 58|
 59|“아직 철이 없어 사고만 치는 녀석들이지요. 한참 부족합니다.”
 60|
 61|“하하, 패화권과 화검봉이면 빼어난 후기지수들인데 그럴 리 있겠소?”
 62|
 63|“과찬이십니다.”
 64|
 65|대답하는 백무성의 입가에도 엷은 웃음이 맺혔다. 비록 첫 만남이었지만 그는 진위경이 마음에 들었다.
 66|
 67|사람을 편안하게 만드는 그 특유의 분위기 때문인지, 철우를 연상시키는 친숙한 덩치 때문인지는 모르겠지만 말이다.
 68|
 69|“이만 들어가십시다. 아무래도 중요한 대화를 나누기에는 장소가 영 적절치 않으니 말이오.”
 70|
 71|“동의합니다.”
 72|
 73|이미 본의 아니게 시선을 끌게 됐다.
 74|
 75|지금처럼 수많은 이목이 지켜보는 가운데 검성에 관한 말이라도 튀어나왔다가는 난리가 날 것이 분명했다.
 76|
 77|“자, 그럼.”
 78|
 79|가볍게 고개를 까딱한 진위경이 앞장서서 걷기 시작했다.
 80|
 81|쏟아지는 시선과 환호 속, 그의 뒤를 따라 걸음을 옮기던 백무성이 멈칫했다.
 82|
 83|뒤따라오는 사제들의 기척이 느껴지지 않았기 때문이었다.
 84|
 85|‘뭐지?’
 86|
 87|슬쩍 뒤돌아본 백무성의 시선에 철탑처럼 우뚝 서 있는 철우가 보였다. 그는 어딘가를 뚫어져라 바라보고 있었다.
 88|
 89|“둘째야.”
 90|
 91|백무성의 부름에 철우의 고개가 스르륵 돌아갔다.
 92|
 93|“예, 대사형.”
 94|
 95|“무슨 일이라도 있느냐?”
 96|
 97|“아닙니다. 아무것도.”
 98|
 99|철우의 옆에 있던 은향이 불쑥 끼어들었다.
100|
101|“아닌데. 철 오라버니가 방금 어떤 사람을 쳐다보던데.”
102|
103|“혹시 아는 사람이더냐?”
104|
105|철우가 대번에 고개를 가로저었다. 그의 두꺼운 몸통이 슬쩍 은향을 가렸다.
106|
107|“그럴 리 있겠습니까? 저야 사부님을 따라 두어 번 나간 것 빼고는 본산에만 틀어박혀 있었는데요.”
108|
109|“그건…… 그렇지.”
110|
111|“갑자기 배가 아파서 측간을 찾고 있었을 뿐입니다.”
112|
113|“그래?”
114|
115|“예. 그래서 드리는 말씀인데, 측간 좀 들렀다 가면 안 되겠습니까?”
116|
117|“소피본 지 얼마나 되었다고?”
118|
119|철우가 짐짓 얼굴을 굳혔다.
120|
121|“큰일을 먼저 보면 작은 일도 같이 해결되지만, 작은 일을 보면서 큰일을 해결할 수는 없잖습니까,”
122|
123|“……어, 그래.”
124|
125|백무성은 마음 한구석이 찜찜했다. 항상 앞뒤 안 맞는 말을 횡설수설 늘어놓던 둘째 사제의 매끄러운 대답 때문일지도 모른다.
126|
127|“둘째야, 너 혹시 다른 생각…….”
128|
129|그의 말은 이어지지 못했다. 어느새 걸음을 멈춘 진위경이 의아한 얼굴로 물어 왔기 때문이었다.
130|
131|“백 소협. 무슨 일이라도 있소?”
132|
133|“아, 아닙니다. 제 사제가 급한 용무가 생겼다고 하기에.”
134|
135|“어떤 용무 말이오?”
136|
137|“그…… 용변을 좀.”
138|
139|“아.”
140|
141|두 사람의 대화에 한껏 귀 기울이고 있던 사람들이 실소를 흘렸다. 철우가 멋쩍은 얼굴로 뒤통수를 긁적였다.
142|
143|“죄송합니다.”
144|
145|“아니오. 본가까지 오느라 여독이 쌓였을 텐데 아예 푹 쉬시구려.”
146|
147|잠깐 고민하던 백무성이 고개를 끄덕였다. 어차피 중요한 대화를 나누는 것은 두 사람이다. 옆에서 하품이나 쩍쩍하게 놔둘 바에야 쉬도록 하는 게 더 나았다.
148|
149|“진 대협께서도 허락하셨으니 그렇게 하여라.”
150|
151|“큰 오라버, 아니 대사형. 저도요?”
152|
153|“그래. 싫으냐?”
154|
155|“네. 전 그냥 대사형 옆에 있을래요.”
156|
157|격렬하게 고개를 끄덕이는 은향의 반응에 진위경이 빙긋 웃었다.
158|
159|“그럼 됐구려. 백 소협?”
160|
161|“아, 네. 가시지요.”
162|
163|백무성은 석연치 않은 얼굴로 걸음을 옮겼다. 하지만 얼마 지나지 않아 훌훌 털어 내 버렸다.
164|
165|‘설마 그 잠깐 사이에 무슨 일이라도 있으려고?’
166|
167|
168|
169|* * *
170|
171|
172|
173|저 멀리 멀어지는 일행을 바라보던 철우에게 태원진가의 무인이 다가왔다.
174|
175|“측간으로 안내해 드리겠습니다.”
176|
177|“측간은 무슨.”
178|
179|“예?”
180|
181|“온통 다 산인데 그냥 길가에 싸면 되지. 안 그렇소?”
182|
183|주위를 둘러싼 사람들이 왁자한 웃음을 터트렸다.
184|
185|구파일방 출신이라 하면 어쩐지 거만하고 무례할 거라는 편견 아닌 편견이 있었는데, 철우의 시원시원한 입담에 모두의 속이 뻥 뚫리는 듯했다.
186|
187|“암, 그렇지. 그렇고말고.”
188|
189|“비록 변방이지만 이 근방이 산세(山勢) 하나는 수려하니 경치나 감상하면서 싸고 오시오!”
190|
191|“이보시오, 패화권! 이리 만난 것도 인연인데 내가 명당 하나 추천해 줘도 되겠소?”
192|
193|철우가 호탕한 웃음을 터트렸다.
194|
195|“으하하! 명당이라, 좋지. 하지만 댁이 싸던 자리에 가기에는 싫소. 그 대신 어디 보자…….”
196|
197|사람들을 쓱 훑어보던 철우가 손가락을 들어 한 사람을 콕 찍었다.
198|
199|“거기 계신 형장께서 안내해 주시는 건 어떻겠소?”
200|
201|아까부터 넋 나간 얼굴로 철우를 바라보던 중년인이 소스라치게 놀랐다.
202|
203|“나, 나 말이오?”
204|
205|“맞소, 당신.”
206|
207|중년인, 우황태의 낯빛이 똥색으로 변했다.
208|
209|
210|
211|* * *
212|
213|
214|
215|“속도 좀 줄여. 여기서부터는 천천히 가자.”
216|
217|“왜요?”
218|
219|“말 게거품 문 거 안 보이냐? 그리고 헐레벌떡 도착하면 누가 봐도 아, 저 새끼 지각했구나. 이런 생각할 거 아냐.”
220|
221|“그거 묘하게 납득되네요.”
222|
223|우리는 천천히 말고삐를 늦췄다. 내려가는 언덕길 아래로 슬슬 태원진가의 전경이 보이기 시작하던 차였다.
224|
225|“그나저나 엄청나게 몰렸네요.”
226|
227|“그러게. 내가 듣기로는 저 정도로 많이 초대하지는 않았을 텐데.”
228|
229|대충 헤아려 봐도 수백을 훌쩍 넘기는 군중들이 태원진가의 정문 앞에 진을 치고 있었다.
230|
231|아직 상당한 거리가 있음에도 작은 환호성까지 들렸다.
232|
233|‘아이돌이라도 왔나.’
234|
235|나는 공력을 끌어올려 귀에 집중했다. 평소보다 몇 배는 예민해진 청각이 사람들의 환호성을 빠짐없이 잡아낸다.
236|
237|그런 내 모습을 가만히 지켜보던 혁무진이 물었다.
238|
239|“무슨 일입니까? 귀한 손님이라도 왔대요?”
240|
241|“화산말학이랑 매화손절이라는데?”
242|
243|“……그게 별호라고요?”
244|
245|“몰라. 그렇게 들렸어.”
246|
247|거리가 꽤 되는지라 듣는 것에도 한계가 있었다.
248|
249|그런데 아무리 그래도 그렇지. 별호가 뭐 저따위냐. 매화손절은 화산파랑 원한이라도 있나.
250|
251|그때 가만히 말목에 엎드려 있던 청풍이 입을 열었다.
252|
253|“은인. 화산일학, 매화삼절이라는데요?”
254|
255|“아, 그래요?”
256|
257|“네. 똑똑히 들었어요.”
258|
259|이 정도 거리에서 그걸?
260|
261|우리 중 가장 고수인 청풍의 말이니 아마 사실일 것이다.
262|
263|“그렇군요.”
264|
265|별 감흥 없이 고개를 끄덕거리는 나와는 달리 혁무진은 말에서 떨어질 정도로 놀랐다.
266|
267|“화, 화산일학! 매화삼절!”
268|
269|“유명해?”
270|
271|“유명한 정도가 아니죠! 화산파 장문인인 천검진인의 적전제자들인데!”
272|
273|“모르면 병신인 수준이냐?”
274|
275|“무인이면 모를 수가 없죠!”
276|
277|“어, 그래?”
278|
279|나는 슬쩍 등 뒤를 가리켰다. 눈을 동그랗게 뜬 청풍이 박수를 치고 있는 중이었다.
280|
281|“와, 별호 멋져요. 근데 어디서 오신 분들이래요?”
282|
283|“…….”
284|
285|“…….”
286|
287|“혹시 소림사?”
288|
289|미친놈인가.
290|
291|무려 화산파 장문인의 막내 사제 되시는 분의 말씀이다.
292|
293|한참 동안 말이 없던 혁무진이 입을 뗐다.
294|
295|“화산일학, 매화삼절. 못 들어 보셨어요?”
296|
297|“화산 좋아요! 매화는 더 좋아요!”
298|
299|“……아, 네.”
300|
301|역시 폼은 일시적이지만 클래스는 영원한 법.
302|
303|‘아빠도 좋고 엄마는 더 좋아요도 아니고 이게 무슨.’
304|
305|화산이 아빠, 매화는 엄마 정도로 머릿속에 입력되어 있는 건가?
306|
307|내가 청풍의 뇌구조에 대해 생각하는 사이 가까스로 정신을 차린 혁무진이 결론을 내렸다.
308|
309|“아무튼 겁나게 유명합니다.”
310|
311|“그렇구나.”
312|
313|“그렇군요.”
314|
315|“……아니, 겨우 그 정도 반응이 끝입니까?”
316|
317|“그럼 어떤 반응을 원했는데?”
318|
319|“보통은 저 같은 반응이라고요.”
320|
321|“말에서 떨어질 정도로 깜짝 놀라야 하는 거냐?”
322|
323|혁무진이 다시 안장에 오르며 열변을 토했다.
324|
325|“그 정도라니까요. 천검진인의 제자! 화산파의 미래!”
326|
327|“그렇구나. 장난 아니네.”
328|
329|나는 청풍을 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
330|
331|“혹시 조부님 되시는 분 성함이?”
332|
333|“매 종 자에 학 자 쓰세요. 매종학.”
334|
335|“별호는?”
336|
337|“검성이요.”
338|
339|“무진아, 들었니?”
340|
341|“네.”
342|

“…”

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 182

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃182화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|저벅. 저벅.
  6|
  7|수많은 사람의 시선 속, 두 사람이 서로를 향해 걸음을 옮겼다. 마침내 마주 선 그들은 상대방을 향해 포권을 취했다.
  8|
  9|“태원진가의 진위경이라 하오.”
 10|
 11|“화산의 백무성입니다.”
 12|
 13|화산파. 그리고 백무성.
 14|
 15|이 두 단어가 가진 파급력은 어마어마했다.
 16|
 17|사방에서 터져 나온 탄성이 적막을 순식간에 걷어 냈다.
 18|
 19|“화산파!”
 20|
 21|“백무성, 화산일학 백무성이다!”
 22|
 23|비록 양민들이 섞여 있다고는 하나, 오늘 이 자리에 모인 이들은 상당수가 무림인이다.
 24|
 25|화산파라는 배경, 그리고 화산일학이라는 별호가 가지는 무게감은 어마어마했다.
 26|
 27|“세상에, 화산일학이 왜 여기에 왔지?”
 28|
 29|“태원진가의 위세가 이 정도였나?”
 30|
 31|“자, 잠깐, 화산일학이 여기 왔다는 건…….”
 32|
 33|정신없이 떠들어 대던 사람들이 주위를 훑었다. 얼마 지나지 않아 백무성의 곁에 있는 일남일녀를 발견하고는 다시 한번 탄성이 새어 나왔다.
 34|
 35|“저 청년이 패화권(敗花拳)인가 보군. 듣던 대로 덩치가 어마어마해.”
 36|
 37|“화검봉(花劍鳳)도 있다! 심지어 예뻐!”
 38|
 39|“우와아아! 매화삼절이다!”
 40|
 41|생각 이상으로 대단한 관심에 철우와 은향이 어리둥절한 표정을 지었다.
 42|
 43|두 사람 모두 몇 번인가 사부인 천검진인을 따라 강호에 나온 적은 있지만 이 정도의 환호를 받는 건 처음이었다.
 44|
 45|“뭐야, 내가 이렇게 유명했나? 별호도 알고 있는데?”
 46|
 47|“철 오라버니, 들었어요? 누가 방금 나보고 예쁘대요.”
 48|
 49|철우가 정색하며 대답했다.
 50|
 51|“잘못 들은 거니까 일절 신경 쓰지 마라.”
 52|
 53|“……짜증 나, 진짜.”
 54|
 55|어린 시절부터 동문수학하며 친남매처럼 자란 두 사람이다. 눈빛으로 으르렁거리는 두 사람의 모습에 진위경이 잔잔하게 웃었다.
 56|
 57|“사이가 좋아 보이는구려.”
 58|

[P91]
“We’re surrounded by mountains. I can just take a dump by the side of the road. Don’t you agree?”

[P92]

[P93]

[P94]
“Of course. That’s right.”

[P95]
“We may be out in the provinces, but the mountains around here are beautiful. Go enjoy the scenery while you take care of your business!”

[P96]
“Hey, Defeated Flower Fist! Since fate brought us together, would you like me to recommend a scenic spot?”

[P97]
Chulwoo roared with laughter.

[P98]
“Ha-ha-ha! A scenic spot? Sounds good. But I don’t want to use the same place you did. Instead, let’s see…”

[P99]

[P100]
“How about that Brother over there guides me?”

[P101]
The middle-aged man who had been staring blankly at Chulwoo all this time jolted in surprise.

[P102]
“M-Me?”

[P103]
“That’s right. You.”

[P104]
The middle-aged man was Woo Hwangtae, and his face turned the color of shit.

[P105]
* * *

[P106]
“Slow down. Let’s take it easy from here.”

[P107]
“Why?”

[P108]
“Can’t you see the horse foaming at the mouth? Besides, if we come tearing in like that, everyone will take one look at us and think, *Ah, that bastard’s late.*”

[P109]
“That makes a strange amount of sense.”

[P110]
We gradually eased up on the reins. As we descended the hill, the Jin Family of Taiyuan slowly came into view below.

[P111]
“By the way, there sure are a lot of people.”

[P112]
“Seriously. From what I heard, they weren’t supposed to invite anywhere near that many.”

[P113]
Even at a rough estimate, well over several hundred people were gathered in front of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s main gate.

[P114]
Though we were still some distance away, we could hear faint cheers.

[P115]
*Did an idol show up or something?*

[P116]
I drew on my internal energy and focused on my ears. My hearing, now several times sharper than usual, picked up every cheer from the crowd.

[P117]
Hyuk Mujin quietly watched me for a moment before asking, “What’s going on? Did they say an important guest arrived?”

[P118]
“Huashan’s Last Crane and the Plum Blossom Cutoff, apparently.”

[P119]
“…Those are epithets?”

[P120]
“Don’t ask me. That’s what I heard.”

[P121]
We were still pretty far away, so there was a limit to what I could make out.

[P122]
Still, what kind of epithets were those? Did the Plum Blossom Cutoff have some sort of grudge against Huashan?

[P123]
At that moment, Cheongpung, who had been lying facedown across his horse’s neck, spoke.

[P124]
“Benefactor. They said Huashan’s Lone Crane and the Three Plum Blossom Elites.”

[P125]
“Oh, really?”

[P126]
“Yes. I heard them clearly.”

[P127]
He could hear that from this distance?

[P128]
Cheongpung was the strongest martial artist among us, so he was probably right.

[P129]
“I see.”

[P130]
While I merely nodded without much interest, Hyuk Mujin was so shocked that he nearly fell off his horse.

[P131]
“H-Huashan’s Lone Crane! The Three Plum Blossom Elites!”

[P132]
“Are they famous?”

[P133]
“Famous? That’s putting it mildly! They’re the direct disciples of the Heavenly Sword True Person, the Sect Leader of Huashan!”

[P134]
“Is this one of those things where you’d have to be an idiot not to know them?”

[P135]
“No martial artist could possibly not know them!”

[P136]
“Oh, really?”

[P137]
I casually pointed behind me. Cheongpung was staring wide-eyed and clapping.

[P138]
“Wow, those are cool epithets. Where did you say they were from?”

[P139]
“…”

[P140]
“…”

[P141]
“Shaolin Temple, maybe?”

[P142]
Was he insane?

[P143]
This was coming from the youngest Junior Brother of Huashan’s Sect Leader himself.

[P144]
After a long silence, Hyuk Mujin finally spoke.

[P145]
“Huashan’s Lone Crane. The Three Plum Blossom Elites. You really haven’t heard of them?”

[P146]
“I like Huashan! I like plum blossoms even more!”

[P147]
“…Right.”

[P148]
Style was temporary, but class was forever.

[P149]
*This wasn’t “I like Dad, but I like Mom even more.” What the hell?*

[P150]
Was Huashan filed away in his head as Dad and plum blossoms as Mom?

[P151]
While I contemplated the structure of Cheongpung’s brain, Hyuk Mujin finally regained his composure and summed it up.

[P152]
“Anyway, they’re insanely famous.”

[P153]
“I see.”

[P154]
“I see.”

[P155]
“…Is that really all the reaction you’ve got?”

[P156]
“What kind of reaction were you expecting?”

[P157]
“Most people would react like I did.”

[P158]
“So I’m supposed to be so shocked that I fall off my horse?”

[P159]
Hyuk Mujin climbed back into the saddle and launched into an impassioned speech.

[P160]
“That’s how big a deal they are! The Heavenly Sword True Person’s disciples! The future of Huashan!”

[P161]
“I see. They’re no joke.”

[P162]
I turned toward Cheongpung.

[P163]
“May I ask your grandfather’s full name?”

[P164]
“His surname is Mae, and his given name is Jonghak. Mae Jonghak.”

[P165]
“And his epithet?”

[P166]
“The Sword Saint.”

[P167]
“Did you hear that, Mujin?”

[P168]
“Yes.”

[P169]
Hyuk Mujin nodded blankly, then snapped out of it. He seemed determined to make us understand just how extraordinary Huashan’s Lone Crane and the Three Plum Blossom Elites were.

[P170]
“Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint, doesn’t count. Honestly, that would be like an adult barging into a children’s fight.”

[P171]
“So what’s your point?”

[P172]
“Huashan’s Lone Crane is already a master who has surpassed the level of a young prodigy. At this rate, becoming the next Sect Leader won’t be a problem. The other two members of the Three Plum Blossom Elites are objects of admiration among young martial artists too.”

[P173]
They really were impressive. From the way he talked about young prodigies, they still seemed fairly young, yet the public already considered them world-class.

[P174]
“Then why am I not particularly impressed?”

[P175]
“That… I’m not sure.”

[P176]
Hyuk Mujin thought for a moment, then his expression suddenly fell.

[P177]
“Come to think of it, I’m not exactly thrilled either.”

[P178]
“Really?”

[P179]
“Yes. Huashan’s Lone Crane used to be my idol.”

[P180]
Cheongpung abruptly cut in.

[P181]
“Isn’t it because of Grandpa Jeok?”

[P182]
“Huh?”

[P183]
“Eh?”

[P184]
“He’s incredibly strong. And he’s trying to take you as his Disciple.”

[P185]
The second part was complete bullshit, but the first part was right.

[P186]
If the Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak, was some unfathomable existence above the clouds, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was a monster who had revealed himself in the flesh.

[P187]
After encountering a monster larger than a hundred-story building, it was only natural that a monster the size of a four-story commercial building would make less of an impression.

[P188]
“And…”

[P189]
Cheongpung looked straight at me and continued slowly.

[P190]
“You’re plenty strong, Benefactor.”

[P191]
“…What?”

[P192]
“I mean it.”

[P193]
Something tickled in one corner of my chest, but he was undeniably right about that too.

[P194]
It wasn’t that I thought I could fight Huashan’s Lone Crane right now without falling behind.

[P195]
*I was certain I could catch up to him before long.*

[P196]
It had taken me only a few months to go from a Third Rate martial artist who knew nothing about martial arts to a Peak master.

[P197]
I couldn’t even begin to imagine how much I might grow in another year or two.

[P198]
To me, Huashan’s Lone Crane was a milestone along the road—not an impassable wall.

[P199]
“Thanks for saying that.”

[P200]
Cheongpung answered with a sunny smile.

[P201]
“You’re welcome. Grandpa said weak martial artists without firm resolve need constant attention.”

[P202]
“…”

[P203]
Fuck me. It had just been a pep talk.

[P204]
I was wrestling with the urge to split open the crown of Cheongpung’s head when—

[P205]
“H-Hey, Young Hero Chul!”

[P206]
“Hah, listen to this old coot calling me Young Hero Chul. Weren’t you calling me an ox-head earlier?”

[P207]
“N-No, Great Hero Chul! I committed a grave discourtesy, *-so*!”[^1]

[P208]
“What was that? *-So*? *So*? Cow? Did you just call me a cow again?”

[P209]
“Eeeeeek! Isn’t that taking it too far? Do you even know how old I am?”

[P210]
“Yes, Elder. Let’s head up there and have a little talk.”

[P211]
A young man with a massive build reminiscent of Jin Wikyung was dragging a middle-aged man behind him.

[P212]
Just as they were about to enter the mountainside beside the hill, the young man spotted us and stopped.

[P213]
“Brother over there, do you need something?”

[P214]
*He means me, right?*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
